title: How to make retries safe with idempotency
subtitle: Prevent duplicate side effects after timeouts
learning_objective: Explain idempotent operations and the role of idempotency keys in retryable APIs.

source_refs.title: Stripe: Idempotent requests
source_refs.supports: idempotency keys for safely retrying requests

scenes.title: DID THE PAYMENT WORK?
scenes.body: The server charged the card, but the response timed out. Retrying blindly could charge again.

scenes.title: A timeout is ambiguous
scenes.body: The client may not know whether the server completed the operation. Idempotency makes repeated attempts for the same logical operation safe.

scenes.title: Design the contract
scenes.body: The server must store and coordinate key usage correctly, define retention, and reject unsafe reuse with different parameters. A header alone does not guarantee idempotency.

scenes.question: What makes a retry safe in this pattern?
options: Using a new random key on every retry
Reusing the same key for the same logical operation
Assuming timeouts mean the server did nothing
scenes.explanation: Reusing the same key lets the server recognize the retry and return the original operation's outcome rather than repeat the side effect.

scenes.title: Remember this
scenes.body: Treat timeouts as unknown outcomes. Design idempotency at the server, not just in the client.
